title: JavaScript, TypeScript, and Angular
summary: Meet the three tools you'll use, and see how they team up.
heading: JavaScript, TypeScript, and Angular

blocks.text: Think of a web page like a body. HTML is the bones that give it shape, CSS is the clothes that make it look nice, and JavaScript is the muscles that make it move. Anything that reacts when you click, type, or scroll is JavaScript doing its job.

TypeScript is just JavaScript with a helpful safety net. You tell it what kind of value a variable should hold — like a number or some text — and it warns you about mistakes before your app ever runs.

Angular is a framework — basically a big box of ready-made tools for building web apps. Instead of building everything from scratch, it hands you components, data binding, routing, and forms. You write it all in TypeScript.

blocks.text: An easy way to remember it: Angular is the toolkit, TypeScript is the friendly language you write in, and JavaScript is what actually runs in the browser.
A variable is just a labelled box where you keep a value so you can use it again later.
